cases.expected: A non‑null byte array of length 12 (the DNS header size) and the Message.size field set to 12.
cases.description: Calling toWire() on a freshly constructed Message that contains no sections, questions, or additional records should produce only the DNS header.

group: Message with a single Question record

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) + the wire length of the Question record. The Message.size field must match that length.
cases.description: Add a simple A‑type question (e.g. "example.com.") to the QUESTION section and verify that toWire() serialises the header plus exactly one question.

group: Message with Question and Answer records

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) + question length + answer length. The Message.size field must equal the total length.
cases.description: Add a question to the QUESTION section and a matching answer (A record) to the ANSWER section. Verify that toWire() includes both sections in the correct order.

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) + any existing sections + the wire length of the OPT record. The Message.size field must equal the total length.
cases.description: Set an OPT record via setOPT() (or addRecord with Section.ADDITIONAL) and ensure that toWire() appends the OPT pseudo‑record after all normal sections.

group: Message with a signed TSIG record

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) + all normal sections + the wire length of the TSIG record. The Message.size field must equal the total length and the last RR must be a TSIG.
cases.description: Create a Message, add some records, then call setTSIG(key) to sign the message. Verify that toWire() adds a TSIG RR at the end and that size reflects the full message length.

group: Message exceeding the maximum DNS wire length

cases.expected: An IOException (or a RuntimeException wrapped by SneakyThrows) thrown when toWire() attempts to serialise a message whose total length would be > Message.MAXLENGTH (65535).
cases.description: Construct a Message with enough records (e.g., many large TXT records) so that the resulting wire format would exceed 65535 bytes. toWire() must detect this overflow and propagate an exception.

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) plus the combined wire length of all Question records. The Message.size field must match that length. The wire format must contain the questions in the order they were added.
cases.description: Add two distinct Question records (e.g., "example.com. A" and "example.org. AAAA") to the QUESTION section and verify that toWire() serialises both questions after the header.

group: Message with Authority and Additional sections

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length equals 12 (header) + question length + answer length + authority length + additional length. The sections must appear in the DNS prescribed order: QUESTION, ANSWER, AUTHORITY, ADDITIONAL. Message.size must equal the total length.
cases.description: Create a Message with one Question, one Answer (A record), one Authority (NS record) and one Additional (A record for the NS). Verify that toWire() respects section ordering and size calculation.

group: Message with both OPT and TSIG records

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose last RR is a TSIG record and whose second‑last RR is the OPT pseudo‑record. The total length equals 12 (header) + question + answer + OPT length + TSIG length. Message.size must match the array length.
cases.description: Add a Question and an Answer, then set an OPT record via setOPT() and finally sign the message with setTSIG(key). Verify that toWire() places OPT before TSIG and that size reflects the full message.

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose length is smaller than the sum of the individual wire lengths of the Question and Answer because the domain name is reused via compression pointers. Message.size must equal the actual array length.
cases.description: Add a Question for "example.com." and an Answer (A record) for the same name. The DNSOutput implementation should compress the repeated name. Verify that the resulting byte array is shorter than a naïve concatenation and that size matches.

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array of length 65535 (Message.MAXLENGTH) and Message.size set to 65535. No exception is thrown.
cases.description: Construct a Message whose header plus records sum to exactly 65535 bytes (e.g., a Question plus many large TXT records). Call toWire() and confirm that the method succeeds at the boundary.

group: toWire with maxLength limit smaller than message size

cases.expected: IOException (or a RuntimeException wrapped by SneakyThrows) indicating that the message exceeds the supplied maxLength.
cases.description: Create a Message whose wire length is greater than 5000 bytes (e.g., by adding many TXT records). Invoke the overloaded toWire(int maxLength) with 5000 and verify that an exception is thrown.

cases.expected: A non‑null byte array whose final RR is a TSIG record containing the supplied error code (e.g., BADTIME). The total length equals header + other sections + TSIG length, and Message.size matches this length.
cases.description: Create a Message, add a Question and an Answer, then call setTSIG(key, Rcode.BADTIME, queryTsig) to sign the message with a non‑zero error. Verify that toWire() includes the TSIG with the error code and that size is correct.

cases.expected: IOException (or a RuntimeException wrapped by SneakyThrows) propagated from the Record's toWire method when Message.toWire() attempts to serialize a malformed record.
cases.description: Create a custom Record subclass whose toWire(DNSOutput) implementation deliberately throws an IOException. Add this record to any section of a Message and invoke toWire(). The method should not swallow the exception; it must propagate it.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException indicating that maxLength must be at least Message.MAXLENGTH (12) for a valid DNS header.
cases.description: Call the overloaded toWire(int maxLength) with maxLength set to 0. The implementation should validate the argument and reject values that are too small, throwing IllegalArgumentException before any serialization occurs.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException indicating that maxLength cannot be negative.
cases.description: Call the overloaded toWire(int maxLength) with a negative maxLength. The method must validate the parameter and throw IllegalArgumentException.
